stories.question: Why do studies disagree about whether pesticide residues on conventional produce are too low to harm health?
stories.whyWatch: Two confident, opposite answers to the same question. Explaining why they differ (population, task, timing, design) teaches more than either headline.
stories.tension: The studies split: Winter and Katz 2011, dietary risk on Dirty Dozen produce says right, Mie 2017 review, health effects of organic food and farming says wrong, USDA Pesticide Data Program, 2024 summary says right.
stories.evidenceNeeded: The studies on each side compared on design, population and timing, to explain the split rather than pick a winner.

Winter and Katz 2011, dietary risk on Dirty Dozen produce: right (0.55, partial)

qualifying.why: the verdict note limits its own scope ("limited to")

qualifying.by: USDA Pesticide Data Program, 2024 summary
